title: Skeletal runway and price-flexion scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, intentionally skeletal notebook for rapid tradeoff conversations: show a minimal set of budget lines, a headcount plan by functional lane, and a compact pricing-sensitivity analysis that feeds hiring triggers and runway deltas. Intended as a working artifact for Finance + Product sync (week 1 of planning cycle).

Context and why this exists:
- We need a quick, repeatable artifact to answer: if we shift list price (per-token/embedding) +/- X%, how many FTE hiring deferrals or accelerations are needed to hold margin targets or runway?
- Focus is on short horizon (12 months) with roll-forward to 24 months for optional upside.
- This doc purposely omits detailed per-feature chargebacks; it provides a lane-level view (Servicing, Dev, SRE, Product & GTM, Support).

Key assumptions (shared):
- Starting monthly revenue (hosted + dedicated): $9.2M (run-rate, Nov 2026).
- Gross margin target (post-GPU direct cost): 70% at baseline pricing and mix.
- Effective blended price sensitivity (demand elasticity): base estimate -0.9 (10% increase in price -> ~9% drop in token volume).
- Average fully-burdened cost per new hire (software/infra/product): $22k/month (annualized ~ $264k) including overhead and stock comp run rate amortization for year 1. For SRE/infra hires use $27k/month.
- GPU cost per token baseline embedded into cost of goods (COGS).
- Target runway: maintain >= 10 months of cash buffer under downside scenario.

Skeletal budget snapshot (monthly, $k):
- Revenue (baseline): 9,200
- COGS (GPU + instance ops): 2,760 (30% of revenue)
- Gross contribution: 6,440
- Fixed Opex (payroll, rent, infra tooling amort): 4,100
- EBITDA (contrib - fixed opex): 2,340
- Monthly cash burn (post capital activities): 1,200 (this assumes some deferred spend in Q1)

Headcount plan (lane-level, hires in next 12 months, headcount delta):
- Serving Runtime (infra optimizations, kernels): +8 hires (SWE infra, SRE mix: 6 SWE infra, 2 SRE) -> incremental monthly cost: 6*$22k + 2*$27k = $174k
- Product & Console: +4 hires (PMs, UX): 4*$22k = $88k
- Developer Experience / SDKs: +3 hires -> 66k
- Customer Success / Support: +3 hires -> 66k
- Research / Applied ML (inference opt): +2 hires -> 44k
- Total incremental monthly run-rate from hires: 438k

Trigger rules (quick reference):
- Hiring greenlight: actual 3-mo trailing revenue >= baseline AND token volume >= 95% of baseline
- Hiring pause: price has been cut > 5% in last 60 days OR 3-mo trailing revenue < 92% baseline
- Graceful slowdown: if elasticity-adjusted revenue drop causes monthly EBITDA to fall below $1.2M -> pause non-critical hires (Product, DevExp)

Pricing sensitivity matrix (concise):
- Variable: list price change | expected volume change (elasticity -0.9) | revenue delta | monthly EBITDA delta | hires impact (months of hiring that can be funded)
- Scenario A: -15% price cut -> volume +13.5% -> revenue delta: -4.35% (~ -$401k) -> EBITDA delta approx -$280k -> funding headcount: -1.3 hires/month (need to defer ~4 hires over 3 months)
- Scenario B: -5% price cut -> volume +4.5% -> revenue delta: -0.45% (~ -$41k) -> EBITDA delta approx -$28k -> funding headcount: negligible (short-term cushion covers)
- Scenario C: +10% price increase -> volume -9% -> revenue delta: +1% (~ +$92k) -> EBITDA delta approx +$64k -> potential to accelerate 0.3 hires/month
- Note: these are blended approximations — dedicated vs hosted mix matters (dedicated customers are less elastic). For runway-sensitive decisioning, reweight elasticity for top 10 enterprise customers to -0.2.

Runway sensitivity (how many months of runway change per price delta):
- Baseline cash runway: 18 months
- -10% price -> runway reduces to ~14.5 months (cash headroom -3.5 months)
- +10% price -> runway increases to ~19.2 months
- Hiring deferrals can buy ~1.5 months of runway per 6 hires deferred (given the monthly savings assumption above)

Quick scenario pack (12-month rolling):
1) Conservative downside (price cut to defend volume): assume -8% price, net volume +7.2% -> revenue delta -0.72% (~ -$66k/mo), adjust gross margin -0.9 ppt -> action: pause non-critical hiring in Q1, delay 3 hires (Product/DevExp), pull $180k/mo in savings.
2) Base (status quo): proceed with lane hiring as planned but with monthly checkpoints and cadence gating per above triggers.
3) Aggressive tightening (margin preservation): increase price +6%, expect -5.4% volume -> revenue delta +0.36% (~ +$33k/mo), action: prioritize infra/SRE hires to lock cost per-token improvements; accelerate 4 infra hires across Q1.

Notes on sensitivity modeling approach and limitations: 
- Elasticity is heterogeneous: small/PLG customers respond strongly, enterprise less so. Current blended -0.9 is an educated midpoint; we need customer-level A/B to refine.
- The model omits churn second-order effects (price change may increase cancellations among price-sensitive cohorts over time).
- GPU unit-cost improvements from infra work are modeled as realized over 3–9 months — early hires have lagged ROI.
- FX, cloud spot availability, and reserved capacity contract re-pricing are material exogenous inputs.

Operational asks (near-term):
- Product + Sales: quick cohort elasticities for top 25 customers (by revenue) by Dec 1. (Owner: Priya)
- Applied ML / Serving: quick quantification of token cost reduction per infra hire (SLO: present conservative / optimistic runbook) by Dec 15. (Owner: Maya)
- Finance: run a per-customer runway sensitivity table and add column for commit-tier vs on-demand mix (Owner: Jordan).

Open questions / decision points:
- If dedicated commit conversion increases by 5% (more committed contracts), how to reassign hiring priority between infra and GTM? Preliminary thought: prioritize SRE + infra to capture unit cost lever.
- Do we enforce price floors for PLG tiers to reduce elasticity-driven churn? Impacts to funnel unknown.
- Timing: which hires are time-sensitive (long lead time) vs optional? Recommend labeling hires in next iteration as critical / discretionary / experimental.

Appendix — quick illustrative calculations (rounded):
- Avg monthly cost for 6 infra SWE + 2 SRE: 174k -> annual run-rate ~$2.1M incremental for headcount additions.
- Deferring 3 hires saves ~66k/month -> ~$792k/year (but some attrition risk).
- If revenue drops $400k/month (Scenario A), cumulative 3-month gap is $1.2M -> potential to defer ~6 hires to preserve runway.

Who to loop in for next iteration: head of product, head of infra, lead of customer success, VP sales (for enterprise elasticity priors), payroll lead.

Draft notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally terse; follow-up workbook will contain per-customer rows and commit-tier multipliers.
- Will import numbers into cost-modeling repo PR #88 and generate visuals for finance sync on Monday.

End of skeletal notes.
